topics.topic: Exact exception types owned by refusals versus deliverer_api
questions: Which exact exception types exist, and which one of `refusals` or `deliverer_api` uniquely owns each type?
Which exact exception types does `refusals` own and which does `deliverer_api` own, especially `AuthenticationRequired`, so that consumers know the authoritative provider?
Which exact exception types are owned by `refusals`, and which are owned by `deliverer_api`?

quotes:
- `DelivererError`, the refusal of a whole operation, whose code is a member of = models.RefusalCode and
  becomes M08;
- `Rejected`, the refusal of one file, whose reason is a member of = models.PlacementFailure and becomes the
  failure of that photo.
- nothing beyond the two exception types; this is shared vocabulary, as `domain_models` is for values.
- `AuthenticationRequired`, the refusal of a request that does not carry the token;
judgement.why: The texts exhaustively assign DelivererError and Rejected to refusals and AuthenticationRequired to deliverer_api.

topics.topic: Ownership of rejecting integer ports below 1
questions: Which module refuses a well-formed integer port below 1, including zero?
Which module owns refusal of a well-formed integer port below 1, such as 0 or -1?

quotes: A8: a required setting is present, an optional one that is absent takes its decided default, and every value is one the start-up table accepts.
A missing required setting or a value the start-up table does not accept ends the start.
judgement.why: The later public-operation contract makes runtime_settings reject a port below 1 because it is not accepted by the A8 start-up table.

topics.topic: Whether deliverer_router directly depends on AuthenticationRequired or the backend exclusively owns the mapping
questions: Does `deliverer_router` directly import and register `AuthenticationRequired`, or does `http_router_backend/v1` own that knowledge so the router has no dependency on the exception's provider?

Must `deliverer_router` directly import `AuthenticationRequired` from its owner to register or inspect this mapping, or is the symbol exclusively known by the backend and therefore forbidden from the router's dependency surface?

quotes:
The router checks no token: the extractor of the `Authorization` field that the backend emits raises
`AuthenticationRequired`, and the router maps that exception to 401 with an empty body, so it imports it from
`deliverer_api`.
judgement.why: The dependency table and accompanying passage explicitly require deliverer_router to import AuthenticationRequired from deliverer_api and register the backend-emitted mapping.

topics.topic: Whether to remove AuthenticationRequired from the no-dependency note or explicitly document the router dependency
questions: Rewrite the negative note without naming the foreign export as a whole word, or make the router's direct dependency intentional and specify it outside a note that says the backend owns the mapping.
Rewrite the note without the foreign export name if the router has no dependency on it, or make the router's real dependency explicit and describe why its runtime code directly uses that symbol.

quotes:
The router checks no token: the extractor of the `Authorization` field that the backend emits raises
`AuthenticationRequired`, and the router maps that exception to 401 with an empty body, so it imports it from
`deliverer_api`.
judgement.why: The foreign name denotes an intentional direct router dependency, so the quoted rule for a note that should not create a dependency edge does not apply.

topics.topic: Boundary between malformed and unknown time-zone strings
questions: What makes a time-zone string “well-formed,” so that malformed strings can be assigned unambiguously either to `runtime_settings` as wrong-form values or to `deliverer_service` as names unknown to the database?

quotes:
| A8 | reading each run setting, its default, and the refusal of a missing required setting or of a value of the wrong form | `runtime_settings` |
| A8 | the refusal of a well-formed port above 65535 and of a time zone the database does not know | `deliverer_service` |
judgement.why: The setting's required form is str, while deliverer_service uniquely owns rejection when the database does not know the supplied time-zone string; no separate time-zone lexical grammar is stated.

topics.topic: Ownership and precedence of startup validation failures
questions: Which module owns the order and precedence between failures found by `runtime_settings` and the semantic port and time-zone failures found by `deliverer_service` when more than one startup setting is invalid?

quotes: Calls `public_op:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings`, `public_op:deliverer_service.load_config`, `public_op:deliverer_service.read_token` and `public_op:deliverer_router.create_app` in that order, then serves the surface on the loopback interface and the `port` of the run settings until it is stopped.
judgement.why: The later public API fixes startup order, so runtime_settings failures occur before deliverer_service performs its semantic configuration checks.

topics.topic: Reachability and required HTTP response for AuthenticationRequired
questions: Is `AuthenticationRequired` truly unreachable dead backend mapping, or can authentication failure reach it; and if it can, must the response be the empty 401 stated here or the M08 `UNAUTHORIZED` response required by A5 rules 1 and 10?

quotes:
No request ever gets that empty answer: the extractor is called by no route the router serves,
and every handler of `deliverer_api` catches its own `AuthenticationRequired` and answers it as M08 (A5 rules 1
and 10), since the health route needs no token and every route that does is a
handler of `deliverer_api`, which reads the field and compares the token itself, before the project id
or the body.
judgement.why: The text explicitly makes the backend's empty-401 mapping unreachable and requires actual authentication failures to become M08 responses.
